title: As prices rose: cuanto más and a medida que

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a medida que* (“as”) and *cuanto más …, más …* (“the more …, the more …”) from B1 Unit 2. Both link two changes that grow together. They suit the social cost of the 1980s, when prices, unemployment and poverty changed at the same time.

items.spanish: A medida que los precios subían, los salarios compraban menos.
items.english: As prices rose, wages bought less.

items.spanish: Cuanto más subían los precios, menos podían comprar las familias.
items.english: The more prices rose, the less families could buy.

items.spanish: Cuanto más se reducían los subsidios, más caro era el transporte.
items.english: The more subsidies were reduced, the more expensive transport became.

items.spanish: A medida que crecía el desempleo, crecía el trabajo informal.
items.english: As unemployment grew, informal work grew.

sections.content: *Cuanto* does not change before a verb, and *más* or *menos* can start either part: *cuanto menos ganaban, más difícil era vivir*. Use *mejor* or *peor*, not *más bueno* or *más malo*. After *a medida que* the verb is in the indicative when you describe what happened.
